title: A Lean formalization of polynomial-latency selfish routing and its potential characterization
claim: For finite routes with 0/1 edge incidence, positive commodity rates and polynomial latencies of degree at most p>0 with nonnegative occurring coefficients, every finite-deviation Nash flow has cost at most (p+1) times that of every feasible flow.
supporting_scope: Nash/Wardrop equivalence for continuous nondecreasing latencies on the nonnegative half-line.
Existence of Nash flows when every commodity has an available route, reusing mrfancypants' accepted Wardrop-existence proof.
Equality of Nash-flow costs and equivalence with global Beckmann-potential minimization.
Corollary 2.7: the integral-ratio hypothesis implies the corresponding multiplicative cost inequality.

formal_targets.contribution_scope: Full equality of total cost for any two actual Nash flows, via Wardrop variational inequalities and edgewise monotonicity. Equality of edge latencies is also checked; existence or uniqueness of flow vectors is not asserted.

Complete existence of an actual finite-deviation Nash flow under half-line continuous nondecreasing latencies, 0/1 incidence and served commodities. Reuses mrfancypants accepted Wardrop existence proof; adds extension and Nash-condition bridges. No uniqueness claim.

Complete equivalence between the actual finite-deviation Nash flow and global Beckmann-potential minimization, with continuous nondecreasing latencies only on the nonnegative half-line. Includes the exact clipped-latency objective bridge and complete accepted predecessor proof bodies.
Complete Corollary 2.7: the Nash cost bound against every feasible flow, under the exact positive-flow integral hypothesis. Handles zero edge flows and avoids division by cost.
Complete Nash/Wardrop equivalence, assembling the two already checked directions from our accepted predecessor proofs. Closes the separately open platform obligation; no new mathematics claimed.

Complete degree-p polynomial latency bound: Nash-flow cost is at most p+1 times every feasible flow cost. All polynomial conditions and the integral estimate are proved from the exact finite-sum definition.

limitations: Formalization of established mathematics; no mathematical novelty, independent human review or source-author endorsement claimed.
The p+1 bound is the source's general polynomial bound, not a sharp price-of-anarchy result.
No route-flow or edge-flow uniqueness claim. The comparison is an inequality, allowing zero comparison cost.
The degree is an upper bound; coefficients beyond p do not occur and leading coefficients may vanish.
The Nash/Wardrop target assembles two previously checked bridge directions; its closure is not new mathematics.
The central entry contains metadata and an original explanatory note, not a self-contained proof archive.
